applies_why: This judge text resolves the Isaiah 7:14 link by relying on whether the sign/verse itself states the mechanism, which is the chain-vs-verse stating-verse issue K-C governs.
quote: the sign itself does not state the mechanism.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: never verse by verse: (1) the judge may note one verse's silence only as part of weighing whole chains by footing; (2) K-C forbids resolving the collision by whether an individual verse states the point. I took the clause as (2).
why: Because K-C requires chain-against-chain weighing by footing and retires any test that an individual verse must state the point, the judge's reliance on the sign's own silence is a breach.
